clue.text: Emperor had managed to cross India

indicators.note: RAN goes across the India letter, straddling it so it sits inside

parts.note: managed means ran, as in ran a business
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone had run a route across the Indian subcontinent.
explanation.definitionFit: Hadrian was a Roman ruler of the second century, famous for his wall across northern Britain.

clue.text: Most good-looking worker, some very holy person too

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand
ST is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: A labourer is the handsomest man around, and a saint besides.
explanation.definitionFit: Handsomest is the superlative of handsome, meaning most attractive in appearance.

clue.text: Prevent bread going bad

indicators.note: bread going bad is spoilt, so its letters are spoilt into a new order

explanation.surface: A tip for stopping your loaf from going mouldy.
explanation.definitionFit: To debar someone is to exclude or prohibit them from doing something.

clue.text: Final action in school period — ten punished

parts.note: a term is a period of the school year

indicators.note: punished suggests the letters of ten are knocked about into a new order

explanation.surface: Ten pupils are given a detention at the end of term.
explanation.definitionFit: Interment is burial, the last thing done for someone after death.

clue.text: Most pleasant characters among Venice's tourists

indicators.note: the letters sit among the characters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Visitors to Venice are judged the most agreeable of tourists.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicest is the superlative of nice, meaning most agreeable or delightful.

clue.text: Grapple with garment?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to deal with or manage a difficulty
second meaning: a long cloak worn by a priest at ceremonies

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests wrestling with clothes; the two parts are separate meanings of one short word.
explanation.definitionFit: To cope is to manage a problem, and a cope is also a long ecclesiastical cloak or vestment.

clue.text: Less than half of characters in college pass

indicators.text: Less than half of characters in
indicators.note: only the opening three of the seven letters of college are kept, fewer than half

explanation.surface: A student scrapes through with below half marks at college.
explanation.definitionFit: A col is a mountain pass, the low point of a ridge between two peaks.

clue.text: Face pain, showing self-assurance

parts.note: pan is slang for face
an ache is a pain

explanation.surface: Someone confronts suffering with poise.
explanation.definitionFit: Panache is flamboyant confidence of style or manner, a dashing assurance.

clue.text: Good Parisian about to become someone important

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the French word is read from its end

parts.note: a Parisian would say bon for good

explanation.surface: A decent Frenchman is on the verge of becoming a big shot.
explanation.definitionFit: A nob is British slang for a wealthy or upper-class person, a toff or bigwig.

clue.text: Attempting to get fish after ordinary food

indicators.note: the fish comes after the food, so it is placed second

parts.note: tack is plain food, as in hardtack ship's biscuit
a ling is a long sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Someone tries to land a fish after a basic meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Tackling a task means taking it on or having a go at it.

clue.text: Walks for chaps with a little man at the rear

indicators.note: the little man is placed at the back, coming last

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for
chaps are men
Des is a short form of the man's name Desmond

explanation.surface: Strolls taken by blokes with a small fellow trailing behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Promenades are leisurely strolls, or the seafront paths where such strolls are taken.

clue.text: Err so badly, making you more upset

indicators.note: done badly, the letters of err so come out in a scrambled order

explanation.surface: Making a bad mistake leaves you feeling even worse.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorer is the comparative of sore, which can mean aggrieved or annoyed.

clue.text: Awfully scared when drinking one cocktail

indicators.note: the shuffled letters take in, like a drink, the one letter
awfully suggests the letters of scared are messed up and rearranged

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A frightened person nervously sips a single cocktail.
explanation.definitionFit: The sidecar is a classic mixed drink of brandy, orange liqueur and lemon juice.

clue.text: Sighed with car spewing exhaust?

indicators.note: spewing throws the letters out in disorder, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone groans as their car belches out fumes.
explanation.definitionFit: Exhaust is the fumes a motor gives out, an emission of waste gas; the question mark admits the stretch.

clue.text: Disrespectful type has come out grabbing king and queen

indicators.note: the rearranged letters seize the king letter and hold it inside
out suggests the letters of come are put out of order

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
R stands for regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A rude person has emerged holding royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: COME rearranged by 'out' gives MOCE; 'grabbing' puts K inside to make MOCKE, and R for queen follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A mocker is someone who ridicules or scoffs at others, showing contempt.

clue.text: Big noise caught having the affair in Paris?

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
in French, l'amour is love, a romantic affair

explanation.surface: Uproar after a couple are caught in a French romance.
explanation.definitionFit: A clamour is a loud outcry or din, like a commotion of voices.

clue.text: Gathers round after end of performance to offer respect

indicators.note: the turned word follows the single letter, so it comes second
the end of a word is its final letter, taken here from performance
round means turned around, so meets is read backwards

parts.note: gathers means meets, as people do

explanation.surface: An audience crowds around after the show finishes to pay tribute.
explanation.definitionFit: To esteem someone is to hold them in high regard, the verb for respecting or admiring.

clue.text: Lead a political party with an explosive start

indicators.note: the explosive goes at the start, ahead of the rest

parts.note: HE stands for high explosive
the DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A party leader takes charge with a bang.
explanation.definitionFit: To head up a team is to be in charge of it, to direct or run it.

clue.text: Surprise opening sale with initial 50 per cent reduction

parts.note: an opening is a start

indicators.note: the first half of sale is cut away, so only its back half is kept

explanation.surface: A shop launches a sale with half off from the outset.
explanation.definitionFit: To startle is to give a sudden shock, a verb meaning to take someone aback.

clue.text: Possess new shelter

parts.note: to possess is to have

explanation.surface: Someone acquires a fresh place of refuge.
explanation.definitionFit: A haven is a place of safety or refuge, originally a harbour for ships.

clue.text: Very little language in a short Bible extract?

parts.note: V is the short form of very
Erse is the Gaelic language of Ireland or Scotland

explanation.surface: Hardly any of a scripture passage is in a foreign tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Scripture is divided into numbered chapters and verses; a verse is a single short passage.

clue.text: U-turning Socialist is no Conservative? Discuss

indicators.note: a U-turn sends the run of words back the way it came, so it is read backwards

parts.note: a red is a socialist or leftist

explanation.surface: A political debate asks whether a backtracking leftist has stopped being a Tory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'U-turning' governs the whole run 'Socialist is no', not just the one word, while the Conservative letter stands at the front despite coming last in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To consider a matter is to think it over or talk it through, close to debating it.

clue.text: Leader briefly turns up, making you cry

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up reads the letters from bottom to top
briefly means cut short, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a boss is a leader

explanation.surface: The boss shows up and reduces you to tears.
explanation.definitionFit: To sob is to weep with convulsive gasps.

clue.text: Looking embarrassed about daughter

parts.note: re is the Latin-derived word meaning about or concerning
D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A parent is flushed with embarrassment over their daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone embarrassed blushes, so their face turns this colour.

clue.text: Some hamburgers about to be served as common food

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the run is read backwards
some of the word hamburgers supplies a run of its letters

explanation.surface: Hamburgers are about to be served up as everyday fare.
explanation.definitionFit: Grub is informal slang for food, especially plain everyday food.

clue.text: Writer meeting tragic woman, a female of many words?

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe was an American writer
Tess of the d'Urbervilles is Thomas Hardy's tragic heroine

explanation.surface: An author encounters a doomed heroine, a woman with plenty to say.
explanation.walkthrough: TESS is the heroine of Hardy's novel Tess of the d'Urbervilles, who ends on the gallows.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who writes poems, wordsmith by trade; the question mark flags the playful description.
